channel.title: BuildLaw: Blog
channel.description: News and explainers on UK construction law: payment reform, retentions, JCT and NEC updates, building safety, adjudication and mediation, explained.

item.title: Are construction retentions being banned? The late payments bill explained
item.description: The UK government plans to ban cash retentions in construction contracts. What the late payments bill proposes, where it stands and what to do now.

item.title: JCT 2024: what changed, and what it means for your next contract
item.description: The main changes in the JCT 2024 Edition explained: Building Safety Act dutyholders, new relevant events, email notices, design liability and what to check.

item.title: Can a court order you to mediate a building dispute?
item.description: Since October 2024, courts in England and Wales can order parties to engage in ADR such as mediation. What changed after Churchill and what it means.

item.title: The Arbitration Act 2025: what changes for construction disputes
item.description: The Arbitration Act 2025 amended the 1996 Act from 1 August 2025. Key changes for construction disputes: governing law, summary disposal, arbitrator duties.

item.title: URS v BDW: why defects from decades ago can still cost you
item.description: What the Supreme Court decided in URS v BDW [2025] UKSC 21 about developers, the Defective Premises Act and the Building Safety Act’s longer time limits.
